page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.126-504 is a high-density compute-oriented instance powered by AMD EPYC 9J45 processors running at 2.7 GHz. Configured on the x86_64 architecture, the machine features 126 dedicated physical cores presenting 252 vCPUs via symmetric multithreading with two threads per core. System memory totals 504.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of exactly 2.0 GB of memory per virtual processor.

The instance does not provide local NVMe or SSD storage, necessitating the attachment of network-based block volumes or external storage arrays for stateful filesystem operations. No hardware accelerators or GPUs are included, directing all computing tasks through the host CPU cores. Network ingress and egress are facilitated with one complimentary public IPv4 address assigned to the host.

Given the high concentration of physical execution cores and a lean memory ratio per thread, the instance exhibits strong qualitative cost efficiency for scale-out parallel computing rather than large in-memory databases. Key tradeoffs include the reliance on external storage latency and the absence of hardware-accelerated vectorization extensions. Optimal workloads include distributed software compilation, batch compute pipelines, parallel CPU rendering, continuous integration runners, and multi-threaded web infrastructure.
